dimensions.note: No credential or secret handling. bdBin is a binary name or path, not a secret; no vault refs needed.

Fixed in 2026.10.15.4: doCheck, pruneWorktrees, unclaimStaleBeads, and cleanTemp now log on entry (projectDir plus dryRun / enabled checks) as well as completion, all with structured placeholders. No sensitive data logged.

Fixed in 2026.10.21.1: `bd orphans --json` prints the literal `null` when there are no orphans; JSON.parse succeeded and the subsequent `.map` threw, turning the clean case into a warning on every run. The parse now goes through exported `parseOrphans`, which coerces non-array output to an empty list and keeps the catch for genuinely malformed JSON. The 2026.10.15.4 behavior is otherwise unchanged: missing bd binary is a warning finding, each bd parse site warns on bad JSON, checkGit throws a descriptive error, mutation methods collect per-item failures, and run() still returns null for optional tools.

Still open overall, but improved. housekeeping_test.ts now has 18 pure-parser tests, including two for `parseOrphans`: bd's literal `null` no-orphans output and a normalized issue record. checkGit, checkBeads, checkTemp, and the three mutation methods remain untested, and there are no failure-path tests. Tracked as a follow-up.
check is read-only and re-runnable. pruneWorktrees/unclaimStaleBeads/cleanTemp are idempotent and dry-run by default; per-item failures are collected rather than aborting the batch.

Addressed in 2026.10.15.4: default-branch candidates now include trunk and develop, and checkGit emits an info finding when `git branch --merged <default>` fails, so a differently-named mainline no longer silently reports zero merged branches. The parsers still read undocumented git/bd output shapes, but every parse failure is now logged (see error-handling), which is the practical mitigation for CLI format drift.
Every Deno.Command is awaited via output() and closed by the runtime; no temp files, sockets, or long-lived handles. du/pgrep/df are optional and absent-safe.
README and examples use generic paths ($TMPDIR, projectDir, extensions/housekeeping) and scoped names; no real hostnames, IPs, account IDs, or internal topology.
All schemas are plain z.object(...) with no .passthrough(); CEL validation works.
All 9 resource/file specs declare lifetime and garbageCollection: audit/git/worktrees/temp/beads/report at 7d, the three cleanup results at 30d, all GC 10.
Not a CRUD lifecycle behavior: it audits local state and performs explicitly gated cleanup, with no create/update/delete/sync surface.
No formal check labels, but each mutating method is dry-run by default and returns the candidate list before any mutation, which is the deliberate guard (notice-and-report posture).

Distinct instance names per spec within a run (audit-current, git-current, worktrees-current, temp-current, beads-current, worktree-prune-current, bead-unclaim-current, temp-clean-current); repeated runs intentionally overwrite the *-current records (latest wins).
No update/delete/sync readback of stored state; methods write fresh audit resources and never read prior versions.

No-op upgrade entries recorded for 2026.10.15.2 (workflow basename packaging), .3 (workflow name quoting), .4 (review fixes), and 2026.10.21.1 (orphans-null handling). The model version is bumped to 2026.10.21.1 so it matches the manifest, which the earlier release had left behind.

mechanical.schema-write-conformance: pass — AuditSchema (projectDir, checkedAt, verdict, errorCount, warningCount, infoCount, findings) is written whole by check(); GitReportSchema, WorktreesReportSchema, TempReportSchema, and BeadsReportSchema each match their write site; the shared CleanReportSchema accepts the prune/unclaim/temp shapes because every differential field is optional. Conditional temp/beads resources are written only when present.
mechanical.truncation-honesty: na — no paginated or result-capped method. The process finding shows the first 5 lines in its detail string, but the full list is retained in the temp resource's processes array. `parseOrphans` returns every record bd emits.
mechanical.instance-name-consistency: pass — each spec has exactly one writer instance name, and no two specs in a run share an instance name.
mechanical.schema-field-coverage: pass — every declared field is written on the path that produces its resource; no field is hardcoded to a placeholder where real data is expected. The 2026.10.21.1 change only narrows the input to `report.orphans`; the resource shape is unchanged.
